Preview matches the exported video.

Removes the background color, image, and ambient wash. Notes, keys, guides, and particles remain. The checkerboard is preview-only. For Premiere Pro and After Effects, choose ProRes 4444 MOV. It keeps full-color detail and alpha; files are larger. WebM is for web delivery. MP4 stays opaque. Some players show transparency as black—composite it over footage in a compatible editor.

If no save-location dialog appears, this browser uses temporary storage for the video. Open Prism in a full tab to try direct file saving. Save your scene settings before switching tabs; imported media must be selected again.

Download MP4

Frame-by-frame MP4 (H.264/AAC), ProRes 4444 MOV (24-bit PCM), or WebM (VP9/Opus) with optional stereo audio. Uses your playback speed and track mix. Choose where to save when prompted. Otherwise, Prism uses temporary disk storage and provides a download. Keep this page open until export finishes.

Use live recording if MP4 encoding is unavailable. Records in real time as WebM or a browser-supported format.

All MIDI processing happens on your device. Your visual preferences are saved in this browser. After the first visit, offline use is available in browsers that support service workers; installation depends on your browser.

Audio can use the local MIDI synth or your own recording. Use the Tracks panel to adjust its offset and timing rate; seek, loop, speed, and export share the same alignment. Imported audio and background images must be added again after reloading. Background pulses follow MIDI note hits. Visual transposition changes the synth, not imported audio. For Adobe editing, enable Transparent background and choose ProRes 4444 MOV. It uses a local software encoder with full-color alpha and optional PCM sound; expect larger files. Use Straight (Unmatted) alpha interpretation in your editor if needed. MP4 export requires H.264 encoding. A local software encoder supplies AAC audio when native support is missing. Video writes progressively to disk where supported; large exports require enough free disk space. Live recording remains available as a fallback. Standard MIDI formats 0 and 1 are supported; format 2 and SMPTE timing are not.

Inspired by MiVi by sunya9. Independently implemented.
